name: Trip positive-conductor supervision
summary: Monitors continuity on the positive side of a documented breaker opening circuit.
description: Monitors continuity on the positive side of a documented breaker opening circuit. A trip circuit carries an opening request from a control or protection device to the breaker operating mechanism. The opening command, the coil supply and the evidence that the breaker opened are separate parts of the drawing.

In a switchgear incomer panel, a protection relay requests opening and an auxiliary contact reports the resulting breaker position. A second trip path can have its own supply and wiring so that a single wiring fault does not remove both paths. For this reference, the drawing identifies “Positive trip conductor condition” at the input and “Circuit fault alarm” at the output. A healthy indication is not a complete functional test.

Trace the initiating contact, protective fuse, trip coil, return conductor and feedback independently. Identify which elements are shared between redundant paths. The diagram explains the intended command path; coil ratings and terminal numbers come from the selected breaker. The functional block is an independent explanation of this named application. Equipment-specific ratings, terminal connections and operating conditions must be established in the project documentation.
readingNotes: Start at the named input: Positive trip conductor condition. Identify its source device or document and the state represented on the drawing.
Follow the named output: Circuit fault alarm. Cross-reference its destination and separate the command from confirmation that the equipment responded.
